beta.body: Odyssey is currently an open beta release. It may behave unpredictably; you may encounter unexpected errors, crashes or sections that are not yet complete.
beta.data: Your progress is kept on your own device only and is never sent anywhere. The one network connection the application makes is to ask whether a new version has been released; you can turn it off in settings. Updates preserve your progress.
beta.feedback: If you run into a problem or have a suggestion, please pass it on; saying which section you were in and what you did is usually enough to track it down.

mistake.assign_to_literal: You cannot assign a value to a number or a string. The left side of `=` must be a variable name. If you meant to compare, use `==` instead of `=`.
mistake.division_by_zero: You cannot divide a number by zero. Check whether the divisor is zero before dividing.
mistake.expected_indent: An indented block was expected after this line. Code under `if`, `for` or `def` must be shifted to the right.
mistake.indentation: There is a problem with the indentation. In Python indentation takes the place of curly braces, so it is not optional. Every line in the same block must line up.
mistake.index_out_of_range: You asked for a position that does not exist in the list. In Python the first item is 0, so the last item of a 5-item list is number 4.
mistake.input_used: Your code asks for input, but exercises run automatically so nothing can be typed in. Define the value directly in your code instead.
mistake.int_conversion: `{name1}` cannot be turned into a number. `int()` only converts text made of digits; letters, spaces or dots will make it fail.
mistake.int_plus_str: You cannot add a number and a string with `+`. Either convert the number with `str()`, or convert the string with `int()` — you need to decide which one you meant.
mistake.invalid_syntax: Python could not make sense of this line. The usual causes are an unclosed bracket, a missing colon, or `=` where `==` was needed.
mistake.missing_argument: You did not pass one of the parameters the function expects. Check the function definition to see how many it needs.
mistake.missing_colon: You forgot the colon at the end of the line. `if`, `for`, `while`, `def` and `class` lines always end with a colon.
mistake.missing_key: There is no such key in the dictionary. Check the spelling; if the key may be missing, use the get method, which returns nothing instead of raising an error.
mistake.module_missing: The `{name1}` library is not installed. The exercise environment only has the standard library plus the packages installed from Settings.
mistake.no_attribute: A `{name1}` has no property or method called `{name2}`. It may be a typo, or you may have assumed the wrong type for the variable.
mistake.not_callable: `{name1}` is not a function, but you called it like one. You may have mixed up a variable name with a function name, or added parentheses by mistake.
mistake.not_subscriptable: You cannot take an item out of this value with square brackets. Brackets work on lists, tuples, dictionaries and strings — not on numbers.
mistake.sql_aggregate_in_where: An aggregate such as `COUNT`, `SUM` or `AVG` cannot be used inside `WHERE`. The reason is the processing order: `WHERE` runs **before** the groups exist, so there is nothing to count yet. To filter groups, write `HAVING` after `GROUP BY`: `GROUP BY category HAVING COUNT(*) > 2`.
mistake.sql_ambiguous: The column `{name1}` exists in more than one table, so it is not clear which you mean. Put the table name or alias in front: `c.{name1}`.
mistake.sql_conversion: A value could not be converted to the expected type — a text column may have been treated as a number, for example. `CAST` or `TRY_CAST` lets you state the type explicitly.
mistake.sql_driver_missing: The SQL Server driver was not found. This exercise runs against an MSSQL server on your own machine, so you first need Microsoft's ODBC driver and SQL Server Express. The first section of the SQL path walks through the installation.
mistake.sql_group_by: When you use `GROUP BY`, every column you select must either appear in the grouping list or sit inside an aggregate such as `COUNT`, `SUM` or `AVG`. Otherwise SQL Server cannot tell which row's value to show.
mistake.sql_no_column: There is no column called `{name1}`. Common causes: the name is misspelled; you wrote text in double quotes (in SQL text goes in single quotes — a double quote means a column name); or you used a `SELECT` alias inside `WHERE` or `HAVING`, neither of which can work because both run before `SELECT`. You can see the table's columns with the **Tables** button.
mistake.sql_no_table: There is no table called `{name1}`. Check the spelling; the **Tables** button shows you which tables exist.
mistake.sql_server_missing: Could not connect to SQL Server. The driver is installed but the server is not answering, which usually means the service is stopped. Open Services in Windows and start "SQL Server (SQLEXPRESS)".
mistake.sql_syntax: There is a syntax error near `{name1}`. The cause is usually a typo, a missing comma or an unclosed bracket; look just before the place the error points to.
mistake.str_plus_int: The `+` sign only joins values of the same type, so you cannot join a string and a number with it. There are two fixes: convert the number with `str()`, or use a comma instead of `+` — `print(a, b)` accepts mixed types and adds the space for you.
mistake.str_times_str: You cannot multiply two strings together. `*` works between a string and a whole number, and repeats the string that many times.
mistake.tabs_and_spaces: You mixed tabs and spaces in the same file and Python cannot tell them apart. Use spaces only — four spaces per level.
mistake.title: What this error means
mistake.too_many_arguments: You passed more arguments than the function was defined to take.
mistake.unclosed_bracket: You opened a bracket and never closed it. Count the opening and closing brackets.
mistake.undefined_name: Nothing called `{name1}` has been defined. It may be a typo, or you may have forgotten to define it before using it. Python is case sensitive: `Total` and `total` are different things.
mistake.unexpected_indent: This line is indented when it should not be. Lines in the same block must line up.
mistake.unterminated_string: You opened a string but never closed it. Make sure the quotes come in pairs. If the text itself contains a quote, escape it or use a different outer quote.

reminder.prompt_body: If you haven't studied that day, a playful Windows notification arrives at the time you choose. If your streak is at risk there's one last warning at 21:30; if you stay away for long, the notifications get less frequent and stop entirely after two months.
reminder.prompt_heading: Shall we remind you of your streak? 🔥
reminder.prompt_how: How it works: so that notifications can arrive while the program is closed, a small task that runs for a few seconds once or twice a day is added to Windows Task Scheduler. Nothing keeps running in the background, no notification is sent while the program is open and nothing is sent over the internet.
reminder.prompt_settings: You can change the time in Settings › Notifications and turn reminders off at any time; turning them off also removes the task.

settings.tour_help: A short tour showing every part of the app step by step.
tour.prompt_new_text: I am Odyssey's centaur. I have prepared a short tour that introduces the app in a few minutes: tracks, lessons, exercises, quizzes and more. Would you like to start? You can leave the tour at any moment.
tour.prompt_back_text: I have prepared a short tour of the whole app; it also shows what is new (levels, the study timer, past attempts). Would you like it? You can leave the tour at any moment.
tour.s_welcome_text: Odyssey is a learning programme that goes step by step from zero to artificial intelligence. Let's look around for a few minutes. Press Next or the → key to go on; leave any time with Skip tour or Esc.
tour.s_rail_text: You move between screens here: Profile, Learning Path, Routes, My Notes; search in the middle, and release notes, about and settings at the bottom. Ctrl+M hides the bar.
tour.s_hero_text: It shows where you left off, your overall progress, how many sections and exercises you have finished and your daily streak. Continue where you left off takes you straight to the next section.
tour.s_tracks_text: Each card is a track: Python, Data Science, Machine Learning, SQL, Mathematics, Time Series… The card shows how many sections you have finished. Locked ones are either not written yet or best taken after another track.
tour.s_section_text: Each section is made of tabs: Lesson, Lecture notes, Quiz and, where there are some, Exercises. A tick appears on a tab you finish. Pass the quiz and solve the exercises and the section is complete.
tour.s_lesson_text: Lessons are written in plain language with examples and diagrams. The list of headings on the right moves you around the section; read to the end and the lesson counts as read.
tour.s_note_text: Write down whatever occurs to you while reading; the note stays linked to that section. Select some text and right-click to quote it in a note. Ctrl+N opens a new note.
tour.s_quiz_text: Every section ends with a timed quiz. Questions come one at a time and you see the explanation once you answer. Afterwards See my mistakes shows the mistakes in your past attempts.
tour.s_editor_text: You write your code here and run it with Run or Ctrl+Enter. The code runs on your own computer and is checked automatically. Start over brings back the starter code.
tour.s_terminal_text: Your code's output, errors and result appear here. If something does not match, the expected output and yours are shown one under the other; if there is an error, 💡 explains what it means.
tour.s_brief_text: On the left is what to do and step-by-step hints; the last one gives the whole solution. When you produce a chart the Output tab opens, and as you try, My attempts: your wrong code and your last correct solution are there.
tour.s_profile_text: Every section you finish and every badge you earn gives XP; as XP builds up you level up. Click the title under your name to choose one of the titles you have earned.
tour.s_badges_text: You earn a badge at important milestones: your first loop, your first model, a whole track… Hover over a locked badge to see how to earn it.
tour.s_activity_text: It shows how much you studied on which day. Studying a little every day grows your streak; if it is at risk I can remind you with a Windows notification.
tour.s_roadmap_text: If you are not sure which track to take in which order, look here: ready-made paths for goals such as Data Scientist or Machine Learning Engineer, with why each step is where it is.
tour.s_notes_text: All your notes are here, in folders by track. You can open your own folders and export or import your notes.
tour.s_search_text: Ctrl+K quickly finds a topic, a section or one of your notes.
tour.s_timer_text: Start a focus round with Pomodoro, 52/17, deep work or your own lengths. The time runs here as a small counter and I let you know when it ends.
tour.s_shortcuts_text: All keyboard shortcuts are here; F1 opens them too.
tour.s_settings_text: Theme, language, sounds, reminders, section lock and quiz time. You can also restart this tour from Settings › Learning.
tour.s_about_text: What changed in each update is in the release notes; frequent questions, the licence and links are in About.
tour.s_end_text: That's all. Press Continue where you left off to start with the first section. Good journey!
